hypothesis: Admit and receipt the terminal oracle-scored trajectories without scheduling the six post-budget trajectory-balance replay updates that cannot affect another proposal, then consume the already queued stop and execute the existing shutdown and direct exit before the evaluator grace expires, while preserving every learning update that influences later graph constructions.
method_thesis: Learn a task-agnostic forward and backward molecular-construction policy from the allowed unlabeled corpus using an atom-and-fragment graph grammar, then restart that policy independently for each objective. From an empty graph, the forward policy samples chemically valid attachment, bond, and stop actions until it produces a terminal molecule; whole corpus molecules are never retrieved, ranked, or used as a finite candidate pool. After each evaluator-announced batch is scored, map each observed score to a strictly positive tempered terminal reward and train on only oracle-evaluated molecules and their sampled construction/deconstruction trajectories using the trajectory-balance loss, a learned partition function, and reward-prioritized replay. Because trajectory balance assigns terminal probability according to total flow across every construction route rather than merely increasing the likelihood of one elite sequence, online feedback amortizes search into a de novo sampler whose probability mass concentrates on high-reward molecular regions while continuing to expose distinct routes to rare high-scoring structures. The optimization target remains the mean final Top-1 across the five independent sessions; flow statistics and replay usage are mechanism evidence, not substitute objectives.

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: direct sampling from a tempered reward-proportional terminal flow distribution
method_tags.learning_mechanism: offline unlabeled construction-policy pretraining followed by online off-policy trajectory-balance updates on reward-prioritized evaluated trajectories
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: trajectory-balance forward-policy sampling of complete molecular graphs from an empty root
method_tags.representation: partial molecular graphs built with atom and attachment-aware fragment actions

task-agnostic pretrained graph-conditioned forward and backward action policies
fresh seeded task-local policy copies and learned log-partition parameter

complete forward-action and paired reverse-deconstruction provenance for every retained trajectory
strictly positive rank-tempered terminal reward computed only from oracle-evaluated molecules
reward-prioritized task-local replay with exact uniform-rank control
sampled plus randomized alternate construction routes with used-route accounting
joint line-searched trajectory-balance updates of forward policy, backward policy, and log Z on identical before/after replay samples
canonicalization, sanitization, evaluated/emitted novelty filtering, and announced-batch enforcement
structured preparation, generation, feedback, activation, and shutdown diagnostics
post-valid-stop flushed shutdown followed by direct os._exit(0) successful-session termination
budget-zero terminal feedback admission with an explicit zero-attempt replay receipt while retaining six replay updates at every proposal-influencing feedback boundary

applicability_conditions: The repair applies only to the terminal observe message whose budget_remaining is zero and which the evaluator immediately follows with stop; no later proposal can consume learning performed from that feedback.

Final accepted and rejected entries still pass through the existing admission, pending-trajectory, reward-refresh, and feedback-receipt path, while every feedback boundary that can influence a later proposal retains the unchanged six trajectory-balance replay updates.

The repair does not change preparation, graph construction, trajectory-balance calculations, reward-prioritized replay selection, reward transformation, novelty filtering, batch sizing, or the existing shutdown and direct-exit path, and it does not claim to repair terminal feedback admission that is independently slower than the evaluator grace.
research_intent.falsifier: The repair is falsified if terminal budget-zero feedback starts any trajectory-balance replay update, fails to emit the final gflownet_feedback or gflownet_shutdown receipt, or any formal task still fails to exit within the five-second stop grace; it is also falsified if a nonterminal adaptive feedback boundary performs other than the unchanged six replay updates.
research_intent.implementation_change: Make train_replay return an explicit zero-attempt receipt when asked to perform zero updates, add an optional update-count keyword to MolecularGraphGFlowNet.observe, and pass that count unchanged to train_replay. In run, compute whether the received observe message exhausts the budget and pass zero only for that terminal feedback, otherwise pass the existing ONLINE_UPDATES_PER_ROUND value of six; retain final-feedback admission, reward refresh, the feedback diagnostic, stop validation, shutdown receipt, and direct successful exit without changing any algorithmic calculation.

research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Algorithm Node n-010ddcf7cfac consumed all 300 oracle calls on each seed-0 objective, but deco_hop produced no formal task score because run synchronously began processing the final budget-zero observe before reading the evaluator's queued stop. Its log ends after all ten generation-29 terminal-provenance records and lacks the generation-29 gflownet_feedback and gflownet_shutdown receipts, whereas the four successful tasks completed the same terminal six-update block, emitted both receipts, and exited directly; the remaining failure is therefore the terminal replay work consuming the five-second stop grace before the repaired direct-exit path can activate.

applicability_conditions: The result is supported for the terminal generation-29 observe with budget_remaining zero, batch size 10, and an immediately queued valid stop: all five such seed-0 sessions admitted their final ten accepted scores, emitted both required receipts, and exited within grace with zero replay attempts.

Every feedback boundary that could influence a later proposal retained the inherited schedule. Across five tasks, all 140 generation-1-through-28 adaptive activation records attempted and accepted exactly six updates; only the generation-29 terminal receipt records zero.

Final accepted-entry admission and reward refresh are supported by source order and by all five final receipts advancing evaluated_terminals and replay_terminals from 290 to 300, with shutdown reporting 610 replay trajectories. Terminal rejected-entry behavior is not empirically established because every final rejected map is empty.

Causal isolation is strong for this bounded repair: the source diff is confined to update-count control, Candidate and Parent use the same prepared artifact content, and all five complete 300-row evaluator trajectories are byte-identical. Preparation, graph construction, proposal filtering, batch sizing, and every preterminal learning opportunity were consequently preserved in the observed sessions.

The clean-exit claim is limited to successful normal control flow on seed 0 and is categorical at the evaluator's five-second threshold. It does not establish exact sub-five-second latencies, cross-seed reliability, behavior when a later proposal follows the feedback, or cases where terminal admission itself exceeds the grace.

observable_measurements.name: post_stop_process_exit_latency
observable_measurements.parent_value: Parent n-010ddcf7cfac has one timeout in five seed-0 sessions. Its drd2_docking, median_2, sitagliptin_mpo, and zaleplon_mpo logs record a generation-29 adaptive activation at line 379 with six updates attempted and six accepted, the final gflownet_feedback at line 380, and gflownet_shutdown at line 381 with 186 optimizer updates; all four task summaries are status ok. Parent deco_hop reaches all ten generation-29 terminal-provenance records but ends at line 378 without the final feedback or shutdown receipt, and its task summary is buggy with 'candidate did not exit after stop'. The exact number of terminal updates completed before that process was killed is not observable, but Parent source line 2243 unconditionally requests ONLINE_UPDATES_PER_ROUND, equal to six, before run checks budget_remaining at lines 2349-2353. Parent therefore explicitly completed six post-budget updates on four tasks and synchronously scheduled the same six-update block on the timed-out fifth task, with final-receipt coverage 4/5 and timeout count 1/5. Its 28 nonterminal boundaries per task also all attempted and accepted six updates. Relative to this baseline, the Candidate's registered intermediate behavior moved in the expected decreasing direction.
observable_measurements.value: The formal seed-0 Candidate satisfies every component of the registered observable on all five tasks. Each zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop, drd2_docking, median_2, and sitagliptin_mpo log has a generation-29 gflownet_feedback receipt at line 379 whose training object records phase adaptive, generation 29, updates_attempted 0, and updates_accepted 0; no generation-29 gflownet_activation_observables event is present. Each log then has one flushed gflownet_shutdown receipt at line 380. All five task summaries and the seed summary have status ok after 300 oracle calls per task, establishing five clean exits inside the evaluator's five-second post-stop grace and timeout count 0/5. The evaluator does not retain send-stop and process-exit timestamps, so individual clean latencies and their exact maximum are not recoverable; the supported maximum is strictly less than five seconds. The terminal feedback path still admitted every final batch: all five final receipts report accepted 10, evaluated_terminals 300, replay_terminals 300, and rejected {}, while shutdown reports replay_trajectories 610. Every earlier adaptive boundary was preserved: each task has exactly 28 generation-1-through-28 adaptive activation records, and all 140 records report six updates attempted and six accepted. The Candidate shutdowns report 180 total optimizer updates, six fewer than the four receipt-complete Parent shutdowns. All five 300-row evaluator trajectory files are byte-identical between Candidate and Parent, confirming that suppressing work after the last oracle batch did not alter any proposal. Terminal replay attempts therefore decreased to zero, final-receipt coverage increased to 5/5, and post-stop timeouts decreased to zero while all proposal-influencing replay boundaries retained six updates.

possible_failure_causes: The evaluator retains only the categorical result of process.wait(timeout=5.0), not monotonic timestamps around stop and exit. The evidence establishes that all five exits were below five seconds but cannot establish their exact latency margin.

Evidence is limited to screening seed 0 under the supplied six-core, one-GPU profile. Different scheduling or device behavior could make terminal admission, reward refresh, shutdown, or another retained pre-exit operation exceed the grace even though replay is skipped.

All five terminal batches contained ten accepted observations and no rejected observations. The unchanged rejected-entry path is source-supported but was not dynamically exercised at a terminal budget-zero boundary in this replica.

The repair deliberately skips only terminal replay. It cannot repair independently slow canonicalization, admission, pending-trajectory handling, reward refresh, stop delivery, exceptions, or nonzero exit paths before the retained direct-exit statement.
